unit.why: A short anecdote: the rebbetzin rebukes the tsaddik for giving money to his enemies and he answers with a homiletic justification, so the narrative is minimal and mostly a teaching.

stories.start_quote: פ״א הוכיחה אותו הרבנות על אשר
stories.summary_en: The tsaddik's wife reproaches him for generously giving money to his opponents instead of punishing them; he explains that the tsaddik is the 'foundation of the world', that he is not himself such a tsaddik, and that he sustains the world by keeping silent in strife, so it is better to stay silent, bear their enmity and keep their livelihood.

quotes: הוכיחה אותו הרבנות על אשר פזר נתן
tags.why: His wife, the rebbetzin, is his interlocutor.

quotes: ושאלה ממנו הלא ידעתיך לאיש מופת
tags.why: The wife acts by rebuking and questioning him, which prompts his answer.

quotes: שמע לקולי יותר טוב לשתוק ולסבול
tags.why: The exchange is a dispute between husband and wife.
He gives money generously, even to his enemies.

quotes: אנכי יודע בעצמי שאינני בגדר צדיק ויסוד
tags.why: He denies being a true tsaddik.

quotes: מי ששותק לשונאיו ואינו פותח פיו
tags.why: The virtue of silence and forbearance in strife is the point.

quotes: והצדיק הוא יסוד הבנין במש״ה וצדיק יסוד עולם
tags.why: The tsaddik as the foundation of the world, which is why people give him money.

quotes: תולה ארץ על בלימה אין העולם מתקיים
tags.why: His answer is an exegetical teaching.
The text is mostly a homiletic justification with a thin narrative frame.
It illustrates the tsaddik's forbearance and humility.

missing_concepts: forbearance / silence toward enemies (bolem atzmo bi-she'at merivah)
money given to tsaddikim as support of the world
